method_selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 8 and then declines while training loss continues downward, indicating overfit. This controlled, zero-initialized residual preserves the fixed champion stack while testing causal session gaps, positions, and one interaction group at a time; it is materially different from the failed standalone hour×tab and weekday×tab openings. Prior Pure results imply an honest expected gain of only about +0.0005 to +0.001, likely below epsilon, but the anchor/session/pair ablations provide high scientific value by separating real session signal from variance before any final ensemble close.

rejected.reason: The plain-field form is measured weak on Pure, and its hour×tab and weekday×tab components already failed as openings.

Although eligible after a tuned package, it introduces auxiliary targets and multiple add-ons, conflicting with the instruction to keep the training stack fixed and attribute the session/context gain first.
It already produced a rejected result in this lineage; replication may later be warranted, but repeating it now would not isolate session structure or the dominant interaction group.
Premature with 15 iterations left and unresolved attribution; ensembling should close the strongest confirmed single configuration rather than obscure whether the current gain is accidental variance.

expected_delta_basis: The selected gated-session-residual card reports only +0.0006 and a grey-rejected 0.6044 on Pure despite a much larger 1K gain, so a sub-epsilon +0.0010 expectation is more credible than its original +0.0018-0.0032 estimate.

method_selection.citation: Wu et al., Stochastic Shared Embeddings, NeurIPS 2019; adaptive sparse-embedding regularization literature.
method_selection.why: The journal reports a validation peak followed by decline, and Pure's small, sparse-ID data makes the added session capacity prone to memorization, although the missing curve telemetry lowers confidence. Frequency-adaptive embedding regularization preserves the accepted training objective, sampling, architecture, and checkpoint policy while testing a focused regularization refinement. Its expected gain is honestly small and may remain below the 0.002 convergence epsilon, but it is low-cost and scientifically cleaner than another bundled search.

rejected.reason: Already measured only marginally on Pure, overlaps the excluded data-shift/flat-signal families, and repeating it would not improve attribution after the accepted session opening.
Changes the objective, contrary to the instruction to keep the current stack fixed and avoid another objective-side opening.
A broad package sweep was already tried on this dataset and obscured attribution; repeating it would conflict with the requested controlled refinement.

expected_delta_basis: Wu et al., Stochastic Shared Embeddings (NeurIPS 2019) and adaptive sparse-embedding regularization report small generalization gains from stronger protection of rare IDs, while the selector explicitly identifies sparse-ID overfit and cautions that the likely gain may remain below the 0.002 epsilon.

hypothesis: Because the parent telemetry is unusable and therefore supports neither an overfit nor underfit diagnosis, replacing uniform BPR pair contributions with current-rank |ΔnDCG@5| weights while keeping the full-session model, pair sampling, 0.5/0.5 hybrid objective, and checkpoint policy fixed will improve validation primary by about 0.0007.

method_selection.citation: LambdaLoss framework (Wang et al., CIKM 2018); component of the public autorec-lab ensemble above.
method_selection.why: The learning-curve telemetry is unusable, so an overfit or underfit diagnosis is unsupported. The clearest remaining test is evaluator alignment: apply nDCG@5 swap weighting to the existing within-user pair structure so training emphasizes pairs that can alter the scored ordering. This is an atomic, literature-grounded mechanism and is untried on Pure. Expected gain is honestly small and uncertain—likely near 0 to +0.001—but it offers cleaner scientific attribution than another bundled architecture or target-side sweep.

rejected.reason: Although metric-aligned and measured successful elsewhere, it already failed in this dataset lineage at 0.601766; repeating it would violate the direction to avoid failed openings.
Its k≈32, long-training package raises memorization risk on small Pure data, and the local listwise family has already measured poorly; it is too disruptive for the current controlled comparison.
It is lower-confidence, may misrepresent validation slates of roughly five impressions, and its expected gain is below the convergence epsilon.

expected_delta_basis: The selected LambdaLoss card (Wang et al., CIKM 2018) identifies evaluator alignment as an untried mechanism but estimates only a near-zero to +0.001 standalone gain.
